title: Composition
summary: Master strong 'has-a' composition where the container owns and controls the complete lifecycle of its constituent parts.
learningObjectives: Define Composition as a strict whole-part relationship with tied lifecycles
Identify real-world composition patterns (Order & OrderItems, House & Rooms, Computer & Motherboard)
Enforce component lifecycle encapsulation inside the owner class
Implement deep cleanup and cascading disposal when the composite object is terminated
expectedOutcomes: You can model tightly-coupled whole-part architectures where parts cannot exist without the whole
You know how to prevent external leaking of internal composed component references

activities.title: Everyday Analogy: The Living Human Body and Its Heart

realWorldMetaphor.scenario: Consider a living human body and its biological heart. The body does not simply borrow the heart from a store on Tuesdays. The body generates and develops the heart from gestation. When the human body dies, the biological heart stops functioning and perishes with it. It cannot live on independently as an active living entity.
realWorldMetaphor.mapping: In software, `Human` COMPOSES `Heart`. The `Human` class instantiates `new Heart()` in its constructor and does not share that private instance with external objects. If the `Human` object is destroyed, its composed `Heart` becomes unreachable and is garbage collected alongside it.
realWorldMetaphor.takeaway: In composition, the whole strictly owns the parts. The part cannot exist without the whole.

activities.title: The Pillars of Strong Composition
E-Commerce Order and OrderItems Composition
activities.explanation: Order encapsulates creation of OrderItem. An OrderItem cannot exist without an Order and is never shared between orders.

stepByStepWalkthrough.description: `OrderItem` represents a line item strictly belonging to an order.
`Order.addLineItem` accepts raw data (sku, qty, price) and instantiates the `OrderItem` internally.
When the order is closed or discarded, all line items are discarded with it.

activities.title: Cascading Lifecycle Management and Resource Disposal
activities.explanation: Microprocessor instantiates its own cores and cascades the powerOff() event to every composed core.

stepByStepWalkthrough.description: No external caller can inject or remove a core from this processor.
When `powerOff()` is invoked on the composite, it cascades down to each core.
Both the processor and its cores are coupled in lifecycle and state.

questions.question: What is the defining characteristic of Composition in OOP?
options: The whole owns and controls the lifecycle of its parts
Classes must inherit from each other
questions.explanation: In Composition, the composite object strictly owns and manages the lifecycle of its component parts.

questions.question: How is Composition depicted in UML class diagrams?
questions.explanation: Composition is represented by a solid filled black diamond attached to the composite (whole) class.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most classic example of Composition?
questions.explanation: If a House is demolished, its Rooms cease to exist. A Room cannot exist without the House.

questions.question: In Java code, where are composed objects typically instantiated?
options: In main() before being passed in
Internally within the composite class's constructor or factory method
In an external XML configuration file
questions.explanation: To enforce exclusive lifecycle ownership, composed objects are instantiated internally by the composite class.

questions.question: Can an object participate in two different composition relationships at the same time?
options: No, an object can have at most one composite owner at any time
Only if it is declared abstract
questions.explanation: In strict composition, a part belongs exclusively to one whole. It cannot be co-owned by another composite.

questions.question: What happens to composed objects when the outer composite object is garbage collected?
options: They become eligible for garbage collection as well (assuming no external leaks)
They are kept permanently in memory
They are moved to another object automatically
questions.explanation: Since the composite held the only references to the composed parts, dereferencing the composite makes the parts eligible for GC.

questions.question: Why is exposing a direct reference to a composed part considered an encapsulation breach?
options: It allows external callers to mutate or bypass the composite's business rules
questions.explanation: Leaking a composed part reference allows external code to manipulate the part directly, bypassing the composite's invariants.

questions.question: What is cascading disposal in a composite object?
options: A technique where disposing the composite automatically triggers cleanup/closing on all composed parts
questions.explanation: Cascading disposal ensures that closing/disposing the parent closes/disposes all internal resources.

questions.question: Compare Aggregation vs Composition: which statement is TRUE?
options: Aggregation is strong ownership; Composition is weak ownership
Aggregation: parts survive whole; Composition: parts die with whole
Aggregation uses private fields; Composition uses public fields
They are identical in bytecode and memory
questions.explanation: In Aggregation, parts survive the whole. In Composition, parts' lifecycles are bound to and terminate with the whole.

questions.question: Why might a composite class declare its composed class as a private static nested class?
options: To hide it entirely from the outside world and enforce that it is only used internally by the composite
questions.explanation: A private nested class guarantees that the part cannot even be instantiated or referenced by outside code.

questions.question: How do you explain the difference between Composition and Aggregation in an interview?
questions.answer: Both are 'Has-A' relationships, but they differ in lifecycle coupling. In Aggregation (weak Has-A), parts are created externally and injected into the whole; if the whole dies, the parts survive (e.g. Department & Teachers). In Composition (strong Has-A), parts are created and managed exclusively by the whole; if the whole dies, the parts die with it (e.g. Order & OrderItems).
questions.expectedAnswer: Both are 'Has-A' relationships, but they differ in lifecycle coupling. In Aggregation (weak Has-A), parts are created externally and injected into the whole; if the whole dies, the parts survive (e.g. Department & Teachers). In Composition (strong Has-A), parts are created and managed exclusively by the whole; if the whole dies, the parts die with it (e.g. Order & OrderItems).
questions.keyTakeaway: Aggregation = independent lifecycle / shared parts; Composition = bound lifecycle / exclusive ownership.
keyPoints: Aggregation = independent lifecycle / shared parts; Composition = bound lifecycle / exclusive ownership.

questions.question: What is the 'Reference Leak' vulnerability in Composition?
questions.answer: If a composite class returns a direct reference to a mutable composed part (e.g. `public Engine getEngine() { return this.engine; }`), an external client can mutate the engine or pass it to another car, violating exclusive ownership. To prevent this, either expose delegating methods (`car.startEngine()`) or return a defensive copy.
questions.expectedAnswer: If a composite class returns a direct reference to a mutable composed part (e.g. `public Engine getEngine() { return this.engine; }`), an external client can mutate the engine or pass it to another car, violating exclusive ownership. To prevent this, either expose delegating methods (`car.startEngine()`) or return a defensive copy.
questions.keyTakeaway: Never leak mutable references to private composed parts.
keyPoints: Never leak mutable references to private composed parts.

questions.question: Why is the Composite Pattern useful in GUI or tree structures?
questions.answer: The Composite design pattern allows clients to treat individual objects and compositions of objects uniformly. For example, a `Panel` can contain `Buttons` as well as other `Panels`, and calling `draw()` on the top panel recursively draws all child components.
questions.expectedAnswer: The Composite design pattern allows clients to treat individual objects and compositions of objects uniformly. For example, a `Panel` can contain `Buttons` as well as other `Panels`, and calling `draw()` on the top panel recursively draws all child components.
questions.keyTakeaway: The Composite pattern treats leaves and branches uniformly through a common interface.
keyPoints: The Composite pattern treats leaves and branches uniformly through a common interface.

questions.question: How does Java's try-with-resources interact with composed Closeable resources?
questions.answer: If a composite class implements `AutoCloseable`, its `close()` method should cascade the close call to all composed `AutoCloseable` parts (e.g. database connections, file streams), ensuring all child resources are cleanly freed.
questions.expectedAnswer: If a composite class implements `AutoCloseable`, its `close()` method should cascade the close call to all composed `AutoCloseable` parts (e.g. database connections, file streams), ensuring all child resources are cleanly freed.
questions.keyTakeaway: Implement AutoCloseable on composites to cascade resource disposal.
keyPoints: Implement AutoCloseable on composites to cascade resource disposal.

questions.question: Why do functional and domain-driven design architectures prefer Composition?
questions.answer: Composition enables building complex entities out of small, self-contained, easily testable value objects. It prevents the deep, fragile hierarchies caused by inheritance, keeping the architecture modular and flexible.
questions.expectedAnswer: Composition enables building complex entities out of small, self-contained, easily testable value objects. It prevents the deep, fragile hierarchies caused by inheritance, keeping the architecture modular and flexible.
questions.keyTakeaway: Composition builds rich domain models through aggregation of focused, cohesive units.
keyPoints: Composition builds rich domain models through aggregation of focused, cohesive units.

questions.question: What are the trade-offs of Composition vs Inheritance?
questions.answer: Composition offers loose coupling, runtime flexibility, and black-box testing, but requires writing forwarding/delegation methods. Inheritance provides direct polymorphism and code reuse without delegation boilerplate, but creates tight white-box coupling and fragile hierarchies.
questions.expectedAnswer: Composition offers loose coupling, runtime flexibility, and black-box testing, but requires writing forwarding/delegation methods. Inheritance provides direct polymorphism and code reuse without delegation boilerplate, but creates tight white-box coupling and fragile hierarchies.
questions.keyTakeaway: Composition trades slight forwarding boilerplate for massive flexibility and loose coupling.
keyPoints: Composition trades slight forwarding boilerplate for massive flexibility and loose coupling.

activities.title: Composition Architecture Checklist
items: I understand Composition as strong whole-part ownership with bound lifecycles.
I instantiate composed parts internally within the composite class.
I do not leak mutable references to composed parts to external clients.
I recognize the solid black diamond in UML class diagrams as Composition.
I ensure composed parts belong exclusively to one parent composite.
I provide delegate methods on the composite rather than exposing internal parts.
I implement cascading disposal when closing or terminating the composite.
I understand how garbage collection reclaims unreferenced composed parts.
I consider private static nested classes for strictly internal composed parts.
I choose Composition when a part cannot logically exist without its parent.

practiceProblems.title: House and Room Composition
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement strong composition between `House` and `Room`. The `House` creates its own `Room` objects internally when `addRoom` is called. Complete `House.addRoom` and `House.displayBlueprint` to output each room's details.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
House at: 742 Evergreen Terrace
 - Room: Living Room (250.0 sq ft)
 - Room: Kitchen (180.0 sq ft)

practiceProblems.title: Desktop Computer and Hardware Components Composition
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Build a desktop computer composition from scratch:
1. Class `Motherboard`: holds `private String chipset`. Constructor accepts chipset. Method `public String getChipset()` returns chipset.
2. Class `PowerSupply`: holds `private int wattage`. Constructor accepts wattage. Method `public int getWattage()` returns wattage.
3. Class `DesktopPc`: holds `private String brand`, `private Motherboard motherboard`, and `private PowerSupply psu`.
   - Constructor accepts `String brand, String chipset, int psuWattage`. It creates `new Motherboard(chipset)` and `new PowerSupply(psuWattage)` internally (enforcing composition!).
   - Method `public void boot()` prints `'[PC: ' + brand + '] Booting motherboard (' + motherboard.getChipset() + ') powered by ' + psu.getWattage() + 'W PSU'`. 
4. In `Main`, create `DesktopPc pc = new DesktopPc("Custom Rig", "Intel Z790", 850)`. Call `pc.boot()`.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput: [PC: Custom Rig] Booting motherboard (Intel Z790) powered by 850W PSU
hints: DesktopPc constructor instantiates Motherboard and PowerSupply internally using new.
Clients do not instantiate Motherboard or PowerSupply directly.

practiceProblems.title: Document and Pages Composition with Word Counter
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Build a document page hierarchy using strict composition from scratch:
1. Class `DocumentPage`: holds `private int pageNum` and `private String textContent`. Constructor accepts `int pageNum, String textContent`. Method `public int getWordCount()`: splits textContent by `'\\s+'` and returns length (if empty string returns 0). Method `public String getSnippet()` returns `'Page ' + pageNum + ' (' + getWordCount() + ' words)'`.
2. Class `Document`: holds `private String title` and `private java.util.List<DocumentPage> pages = new java.util.ArrayList<>()`.
   - Constructor initializes title.
   - Method `public void addPage(String content)`: instantiates a new page internally with `pages.size() + 1` as pageNum.
   - Method `public void printDocumentStats()`: prints `'Document: ' + title + ' [' + pages.size() + ' pages]'`. Then prints each page snippet indented with `' > ' + snippet`. Then prints `'Total Words: ' + totalWords`.
3. In `Main`, create document 'OOP Design Manual'. Add page 'Inheritance is powerful but easily misused'. Add page 'Favor object composition over class inheritance'. Call `printDocumentStats()`.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Document: OOP Design Manual [2 pages]
 > Page 1 (6 words)
 > Page 2 (6 words)
Total Words: 12
hints: Document creates DocumentPage instances internally in addPage.
Split by "\\s+" counts words separated by spaces.

practiceProblems.title: Bug Hunt: Leaking Internal Composed Heart Reference
practiceProblems.problemStatement: A developer wrote a `Robot` class that composes a `RobotBattery`. However, the developer wrote `public RobotBattery getBattery() { return this.battery; }`, allowing an external caller to directly drain and tamper with the battery from outside! Fix `Robot` to encapsulate the battery properly: remove `getBattery()`, provide a delegated `public void charge(int amount)` and `public int getChargeLevel()` method instead.
hints: Add getSerialNumber(), charge(int amt), and getChargeLevel() delegation methods on Robot.

practiceProblems.title: Cascading Database Transaction Unit-of-Work
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Build a transactional database unit-of-work with cascading composition from scratch:
1. Class `TransactionLog`: holds `private java.util.List<String> entries = new java.util.ArrayList<>()`. Method `public void record(String action)` adds action to entries. Method `public void flush()` prints `'Flushing ' + entries.size() + ' audit log entries'` and clears entries.
2. Class `ConnectionPool`: holds `private int activeConnections`. Method `public void open()`: activeConnections = 3; prints `'Opened 3 DB connections'`. Method `public void closeAll()`: activeConnections = 0; prints `'Closed all DB connections'`.
3. Class `DatabaseTransactionManager`: composes `TransactionLog` and `ConnectionPool` directly (instantiated in constructor). Also holds `private String txId`.
   - Constructor initializes txId, creates new TransactionLog and ConnectionPool.
   - Method `public void begin()`: prints `'=== Transaction ' + txId + ' BEGIN ==='` and calls connectionPool.open().
   - Method `public void executeOp(String op)` calls transactionLog.record(op).
   - Method `public void commit()`: prints `'Committing transaction ' + txId`. Calls transactionLog.flush(). Calls connectionPool.closeAll(). Prints `'=== Transaction ' + txId + ' END ==='`.
4. In `Main`, create manager 'TX-770'. Call `begin()`. Execute ops 'INSERT User (Alice)' and 'UPDATE Balance (Alice, 500)'. Call `commit()`.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
=== Transaction TX-770 BEGIN ===
Opened 3 DB connections
Committing transaction TX-770
Flushing 2 audit log entries
Closed all DB connections
=== Transaction TX-770 END ===
hints: DatabaseTransactionManager instantiates both TransactionLog and ConnectionPool internally.
commit() cascades to log.flush() and pool.closeAll() in sequence.
